chunks: When a man hears the testimony, and he was not called as a witness upon it, then he is free to choose: if he desires, he testifies, and if he desires, he remains silent.

key_terms.الشَّهَادَةَ: testimony (shahadah) — the formal act of bearing witness in a legal or religious context; distinct from the shahada (declaration of faith)
key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: with the choice (bil-khiyar) — a jurisprudential term indicating discretionary permission rather than obligation or prohibition
key_terms.يُشْهَدْ: to be called as witness — the passive form indicates formal request or appointment as a witness, as opposed to merely overhearing

ai.seo_question: Is a person who overhears testimony obligated to testify in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a permissive legal ruling regarding testimony: a person who happens to hear testimony but was not formally requested to serve as a witness bears no religious obligation to come forward and testify. This ruling provides important flexibility in early Islamic legal practice, where social pressure might otherwise compel uninvited witnesses to testify. The ruling affirms individual discretion in voluntary testimony, distinguishing it from the mandatory duty that falls on those formally summoned to bear witness.
